projects.title: Show HN: Linting 216 public Claude Code skills – 69% won't reliably trigger
projects.author: sgharlow
projects.summary: I built a linter for Claude Code artifacts (skills, subagents, slash commands, .mcp.json configs, and plugins) and then pointed it at a pile of public repos to see what people actually ship. A few of the numbers surprised me enough that I wrote them up. The one that stuck: across 87 public subagents, 57% (50 of 87) declare no `tools` list at all. That reads like a safe default, but it's the opposite. A subagent with no `tools` inherits the caller's entire toolbox, Bash included. Permission prompts still gate execution, but a worker you meant to "just read code" now carries the grant surface to run shell — the opposite of least-privilege. Add 16 more that grant bare `Bash` and 8 that grant a wildcard, and 85% of the sample isn't least-privilege. Other findings from the two scans: - Of 215 public skills scored for triggering, 69% have a `description` that won't reliably trigger (40% outright unlikely to fire, 28% borderline). "My skill never fires" is the #1 real-world failure, and it hides in one frontmatter line. - 83% of subagents (72 of 87) lack invocation cues ("use when…") in their description. - 1 of 216 skills, and 0 of 87 subagents, pass every check cleanly. Almost everyone got secrets right: only 6 of 216 skills tripped the scanner. How it works: mostly pure, deterministic checks that emit file:line evidence ("SKILL.md:14 links ./references/converter.md, not found"). An optional LLM check (bring your own key) judges whether a description will actually trigger. The CLI is free (`npx skillcrossroads ./my-skill`), there's a GitHub Action that gates PRs, and it's open-core: the public audits are free, money is a hosted Pro tier. Limits: the two reports ran different editions (skills on rubric v1.2 with the LLM checks, agents on v1.2 deterministic-only), both labeled, tree SHAs pinned, reproduction commands published. The rubric is strict on purpose, and every finding carries file:line evidence you can check against the artifact itself. The sample is 216 skills across 18 repos and 123 agents/commands (87 subagents + 36 commands) across 10 repos, caps disclosed, and you can re-run it on your own repos. Reports: https://skillcrossroads.com/report?ref=hn-show and https://skillcrossroads.com/report-agents?ref=hn-show Code: https://github.com/sgharlow/skillcrossroads

projects.title: Ring for Me
projects.summary: Ring for Me calls businesses for you to ask questions, check availability and make bookings. Use the web app or connect your AI assistant via MCP. Approve a spending cap, then get the outcome and transcript. Available in New Zealand and Australia.

projects.title: Altifigence
projects.summary: Altifigence is an AI-native platform for chip and electronics design. Write SystemVerilog, explore circuits, and review simulation and verification results in one workspace. CLI and MCP interfaces let AI agents work with engineering tools, not just generate code. Built for students, independent engineers, and small teams looking for accessible tools without enterprise pricing.

projects.title: Edgee Codex Compressor V2
projects.summary: We benchmarked Codex alone against Codex routed through Edgee's compression gateway on the same repo, with the same model, under the same workflow. The result: Codex + Edgee used 49.5% fewer input tokens, improved cache hit rate from 76.1% to 85.4%, and reduced total session cost by 35.6%. This post breaks down why context compression makes Codex more efficient, more frugal, and materially cheaper to run without sacrificing useful output.

projects.title: Boundless
projects.summary: Tell your agent what you want done. Boundless lets it work with APIs without you reading docs or writing integrations. Your agent figures out the details, you grant access, and useful workflows become tools you can use again.

projects.title: klemm
projects.summary: Turn a photo or idea into a brick model, step-by-step building guide and parts list. klemm is a local skill for your AI agent, optimized for GPT-6 Astra in Codex. Get 3D files, renders, PDF instructions and a portable ZIP.

projects.title: Performant
projects.summary: Performant puts an agent between your clients and their website or app codebase, turning requests into prompts for your team or coding agent. Clients explain their changes or requests in plain English and our patient intake agent uses project and codebase context to confirm the scope. Your team gets a structured brief and prepared engineering prompt to pull into Codex through MCP, build in its own setup, and return for review. Progress, updates, and approval stay together under your brand.

projects.title: SkyTwin
projects.summary: SkyTwin: personal AI you can inspect, question, and run locally. It models preferences, explains itself, and gates actions behind a policy layer. Apache-2.0. Local by default—no silent remote fallback. Early preview, not a finished agent. Start with the screenshot walkthrough, then the fictional-data sample (no inbox, no key, can’t touch real accounts). Site has guides plus architecture/MCP docs. Feedback wanted on review-and-correct, what it should remember, and where it must ask first.

projects.title: GenioOne
projects.summary: GenioOne Community Edition is a source-first control plane for teams bringing AI agents into real work. Connect models, MCP servers, APIs, and knowledge; apply policy through the gateway; and give agents governed access on infrastructure you control. Join the commercial edition waitlist for broader enterprise rollout.

projects.title: Godot MCP Studio
projects.summary: Godot MCP Studio connects Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline and other MCP clients to the Godot 4 editor. Your AI can inspect and edit scenes, nodes, scripts, animations, tilemaps and shaders, run the game, read errors and fix them. One-click setup, safe permission modes, undo support, and everything runs locally. Pro adds 346+ tools, templates and Image Studio for pixel art, sprites and animations. Start free with Lite on Windows and macOS.

projects.title: AgenKit
projects.summary: A full team of specialist AI coding agents and the /agenkit workflow for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Agentic coding with local memory that cuts tokens.

projects.title: Mela
projects.summary: Pick a game and play—no download or signup wall. Mela brings 18 browser games into one shared playground: play solo, invite friends, bring an AI agent to supported games, or join the crowd and influence the match. Run a three-game Circuit with your group, join by QR, and revisit scorecards, clips and playable memories. WebMCP and remote MCP let agents take part under the same game rules. Eighteen games is just the start.

projects.title: Bilaga
projects.summary: Your AI agent made a 40 GB file. Now what? Bilaga lets agents send and collect large files with one API or MCP call. They get a share link, the recipient needs no account, and each transfer gets a signed receipt. 5 free transfers a month, no subscription.

projects.title: HypeStreet
projects.summary: Start with 10,000 HypeBucks and buy shares in your favorite AI models, characters, and celebrities. Player trades move prices. Build your portfolio and see how you rank. No real money or cash-out. Gameplay demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8JQF-Mi5zZA WebMCP tools are available for compatible browser agents.

projects.title: Synapse Channel
projects.summary: SYNAPSE CHANNEL is a local-first, vendor-neutral coordination layer for independent AI agents working across terminals, repositories and projects. It provides presence, lease-based work claims, shared tasks, messaging, handoffs, resources and durable history. Use the open Core locally, connect existing agents through MCP/A2A or terminal adapters, and extend to production multi-hub deployments with Fleet.

projects.title: Show HN: Skillmem – local memory for coding agents that stores how, not what
projects.author: mrPetrukovich

projects.title: BetaDrop.app
projects.summary: BetaDrop turns an iOSipa or Androidapk into an over-the-air install link and QR code; testers install from their phone's browser, no TestFlight or Play Store. New since our first launch: per-link passwords, expiry by time, downloads or unique devices, build-level revocation, ClamAV scanning, tester feedback and analytics, UDID collection, stable channel URLs (Pro), white-label install pages (Studio), a GitHub Action, and an MCP server for AI coding agents.

projects.title: TestMyVibe
projects.summary: Discover user flows, audit source code, and review human-approved AI fixes in a pTestMyVibe is an MCP server that lets AI coding agents audit and test your application. Connect it to tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or VS Code via the Model Context Protocol, and your agent will map features into a graph, generate real user journeys, and verify each step against your actual source. The dashboard raises fixable issues with file references, supports human approval, and tracks work on a kanban.

projects.title: Lottieditor
projects.summary: Create and edit Lottie animations in your browser. Or use the MCP to let your agents make them for you.

projects.title: Design Arc
projects.summary: Design Arc is a Codex plugin that turns vague product feedback into a complete, evidence-backed design direction. It confirms the outcome, audits the real user journey, checks decisions against official platform guidance and optional Mobbin benchmarks, recommends the strongest path, and designs every important state before implementation. Human approval gates preserve control, while optional Google Stitch exploration helps teams compare and refine visual proposals.

projects.title: Frely CLI
projects.summary: FrelyMCP lets browser agents and command-line agents such as Codex and Claude Code access your device's files, commands and processes through remote HTTP MCP with OAuth.

projects.title: Matchaboy — Good games. Greener days.
projects.summary: Matchaboy turns handheld gaming into hands-on discovery. Play Game Boy and Game Boy Advance games, then pause and explore CPU instructions, memory, graphics and sound through a built-in Inspector. Free and open source, with two included indie games and direct host/join netplay. Built with Astra in Codex: an original Game Boy engine, mGBA-powered GBA support, and ten original game experiments available in the source.

projects.title: Metricanic
projects.summary: Metricanic tracks clicks, conversions, events and costs from all your ad sources (Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, ad networks) in one account. Ask AI which ads lose money, and let it act on the answer: the built-in MCP server lets AI read your reports, re-route visitors by country, device or OS, and change campaign settings for you.

projects.title: Evidra — The research harness
projects.summary: Evidra gives research agents durable memory, parallel exploration, and experimental rigor. Independent agent lanes investigate competing ideas and share discoveries. Failed hypotheses inform future attempts, evidence stays linked to its sources, and replication gates check promising results. Adaptive recovery changes approach after failures, while checkpoints let campaigns resume across sessions. One harness for open-ended research and measurable challenges.

projects.title: InboxJoy
projects.summary: Connect unlimited domains and inboxes. InboxJoy rotates sending across them automatically and watches bounce rates — if an inbox starts bouncing, it stops sending from it before your domain gets burned. Connect Gmail or Outlook in one click. Upload a CSV. No dedicated domains, no DNS, no ops layer. Also works entirely from Claude/ChatGPT via MCP. $25/mo flat, unlimited access. 7-day free trial.

projects.title: ToolBraid Companion
projects.summary: Built for developers. Bring your existing Codex or MCP session into live pages, native WebMCP tools on compatible sites, Windows controls and approved files. Collect source-linked research, run checkpointed workflows and handle community replies without starting another AI conversation. Optional browser chat uses your ChatGPT account through Codex. Free, open source and available now as a functional Windows release candidate.

projects.title: LabSpace Atlas
projects.summary: LabSpace Atlas brings lab planning and organization into one browser workspace. Design rooms in synchronized 2D/3D, explore 115 laboratory assets, track stock and expiry dates, assign items to named shelves and drawers, and navigate to exact locations. Validate placements, review collection plans, and save or export your workspace. Optional WebMCP tools let a browser agent assist with planning and searches while you control approvals. The public demo saves each visitor's work in their browser.

projects.title: HORS
projects.summary: CORS for AI agents. A browser asks which origin is this request from?; HORS asks which human is behind the agent making this call? — and answers with an anonymous, unforgeable World ID identity, so an MCP server or HTTP API can say "only my own human", "any verified human", or anything in between, without accounts, API keys or shared secrets.

projects.title: Alongside
projects.summary: Alongside helps you learn better AI workflows while building in Codex or Claude Code. Get practical guidance on prompts, context and debugging, understand why another approach may help, and save useful lessons privately in your project. Learn through the work you’re already doing.

projects.title: Mingle
projects.summary: Mingle is an open-source network where AI agents help their people find each other. Tell your agent who you want to meet, approve the exact card it publishes, and let other agents find relevant people. No profiles to browse, no feed, and no ranking people. Introductions are double opt-in, and contact details are released only after both sides choose to share. Works with Claude, Cursor, OpenClaw, and any MCP client.

projects.title: Rill
projects.summary: Your agent says it works. See for yourself. Rill records your AI agent’s browser run with video, console logs, network requests, and an interaction timeline. Replay the flow, investigate failures, and share the whole run in one link. Use it to review a fix before shipping, attach evidence to a pull request, or give the next person or agent the context to continue.

projects.title: SRIFT
projects.summary: Send files securely with client-side AES-256-GCM encryption and zero cloud storage. Direct P2P transfer, encrypted chat, and native MCP tools for humans and AI.

projects.title: DecisionGraph
projects.summary: DecisionGraph traces the evidence behind AI decisions, blocks stale approvals, and requires a fresh review when data changes. Try the no-signup recall demo. Built with GPT-6 Astra in Codex; open source, with DataHub integration.

projects.title: Caelis
projects.summary: Caelis is an open-source, terminal-first runtime for long-running AI agent work. Run GPT-6 Astra as the lead agent and bring specialist models and ACP agents into the same local session. Participants exchange messages, use tools, and keep their own conversations. Follow their work in split panes, steer agents directly, and resume durable sessions with built-in memory and approval controls.

projects.title: Show HN: An open Add/Search evaluation framework for agent memory
projects.author: IreneAI
projects.summary: Hi HN, We are trying to make different Agent Memory systems comparable without letting each team choose its own answer model and evaluation pipeline.

projects.title: ClicData MCP
projects.summary: ClicData MCP Server: bring your BI data into any AI chat. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity and other MCP-compatible clients directly to ClicData. Ask any questions on live data, and pull dashboards without leaving the conversation. Phase one covers data & dashboard retrieval; next up: letting your AI client build dashboards and Data Flows on its own. No exports, no new pipelines, just your data, where you're already working!

projects.title: Opportunity Scout
projects.summary: Find active hackathons, grants and developer gigs. Compare source-confirmed cash prizes and deadlines, save a shortlist, and ask an OpenAI advisor what fits your skills and schedule. Built with GPT-6 Astra in Codex.

projects.title: NovelOS
projects.summary: NovelOS is an open-source multi-agent system for long-form creation. It coordinates 11 specialized agents and 16 skills, with shared state, model routing, deterministic continuity checks, and a canonical state ledger designed to keep long-running creative workflows consistent.

projects.title: Integrated Architecture Environment
projects.summary: Design systems, collaborate with your teammates, let AI agents take control through WebMCP.

projects.title: Insacheck
projects.summary: Insacheck is HR software for small businesses in Korea. Employees clock in from their phone with GPS, NFC stickers or QR, request leave by the hour, and sign employment contracts digitally. Managers see who is working, approve leave, and run multiple branches in one place. Every core feature is free with no seat limits and no credit card. It also connects to ChatGPT and Claude over MCP, so you can ask "who clocked in today?" in plain language, with tools scoped by role.

projects.title: Unfetch.com
projects.summary: Unfetch connects Google Ads, Analytics, and Search Console to the AI tools you already use. It gives ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI clients the live evidence they need to provide useful marketing answers. Use it for reporting, optimizations, alerts, monitoring and more. Works via a hosted MCP or an agent plugin (one click install)

projects.title: mcp-writ
projects.summary: mcp-writ aims to support allowlist-based operation of local MCP servers by combining static analysis for policy drafting with runtime JSON-RPC checks and OS sandboxing.

projects.title: Show HN: Bastionskill – scan an AI agent skill for malicious code
projects.author: Rinkia

projects.title: Bench
projects.summary: Bench is a native Mac video editor built for AI agents through MCP. Finally models are capable of doing the grunt work of sliders and button pressing. Now you can focus on the creativity. Built the ground up for agent gets precise editing tools, this is an agent first editor. Local rendering using fast swift and metal frameworks allows for NLE class colour adjustments, video formats, framing and audio fades and more. Finish in Bench or export to Final Cut or Resolve.

projects.title: Kodro
projects.summary: Kodro is an offline robot studio for UK Computing, KS1 to KS4. Pupils design a rover, write real code, and run it through simulated worlds, getting pass/fail evidence with telemetry on every run. NEW: Genesis races up to 4 controllers through seeded contracts and proves the winner. Built for reasoning agents: Astra can drive the full loop over MCP, reading code, running it, grading it, iterating, while Kodro holds verdicts no model can fake. Honest kinematic sim, MIT open source.

projects.title: Show HN: Concat: the open-source CapCut replacement.
projects.author: calanus
projects.summary: I started this project about ~3 weeks ago. Since CapCut is putting everything behind a paywall after gaining millions of installs and users, I decided to create a free and open-source version with most if not all the features. Concat runs all the AI-features locally, has MCP support, has a decentralized system for assets like Filters, Effects, and Templates so users can write custom assets and share with the community (or sell them even). Note: I’m self-taught dev and used Claude (Fable 5.1) heavily while building Concat.

projects.title: mAIn Human
projects.summary: mAIn human is one AI to talk to. It's a 3D digital person on your Windows desktop. The first character is Ed. Two things make it more than a chat buddy: 1. It's the middleman. You talk to Ed; he routes the work to Claude, Codex, GPT and reports back. 2. It's the context layer. mAIn human is wired into your memory, so every task goes out with the context it needs and comes back with what actually happened. Today mAIn human is free to claim. Pricing comes after launch.

projects.title: VECTA
projects.summary: Start a coding task on your work computer. Review it from your laptop. Answer the agent from your phone. VECTA brings supported agents, projects, chats, code reviews and teammates into one workspace. Bring your own AI account or compatible local models, add skills, and manage task permissions and budgets. VECTA Cloud supports conversations and generated files without a connected PC. Free during private beta; access by approval.

projects.title: Sourceant
projects.summary: SourceAnt connects your code, the services it depends on, and the decisions behind it. It brings that context into code reviews and your agents’ work, so every change builds on what your team already knows.

projects.title: Synapse MCP + GPT-6 on Steroids
projects.summary: GPT-6 Astra is the most capable coding model ever built. That only matters if it knows how your code is put together. Without Synapse, it's a talented junior — grep, guess, pray the build passes. With Synapse? Astra is a confident senior engineer. Synapse MCP is the structural brain: a local AST graph, 50+ languages, instant caller trees, edits simulated before they land. 60% fewer tokens. 2.2x faster. No babysitting. Astra reasons; Synapse knows how all of your code is built. Fast. Local. Free.

projects.title: Swarm
projects.summary: I've been working on Swarm since March exclusively with OpenAI's models and I always use their latest releases for the core of development. Swarm allows for the creation of Spaces where agents/humans can collaborate and store persisted data/memory in Decision Graphs. Swarm is model agnostic and supports both local runtimes and cloud hosted agents. You can also connected cross Space agents giving Swarm a network and essentially providing an intelligence substrate for agents.

projects.title: Spellcast
projects.summary: Spellcast was built with GPT-6 Astra. I used Astra heavily to design and ship the desktop stage: passive bubbles for side thoughts, an editable Canvas for results, and completion notices when a turn ends. That burned through my Astra Pro 20x before launch day. Runtime target today: Codex on Windows (MCP + hooks). Local-first, open source, EN/中文 UI. The clip shows one host path; the core idea is the desktop stage around the agent.

projects.title: Projects by Wornpage
projects.summary: Projects keeps owners, blockers, next actions, and evidence of completion together. Organize your work, see what's next, and what needs attention. Connect supported AI agents through MCP so people and agents can work from the same tracked context.

projects.title: Funny Guys
projects.summary: Funny Guys is a fast-paced multiplayer party game where players race through chaotic obstacle courses, survive mini-games, and compete to be the last one standing. Recently, we’ve been using GPT-6 Astra across development: creating character concepts, building a 148-character 3D pipeline with Blender MCP, rebuilding the entire UI, improving bot feedback, expanding online play, analyzing bugs, and preparing new maps.

projects.title: ProductBridge
projects.summary: Most teams run a helpdesk, a feedback board and a survey tool, then copy between them all week. ProductBridge is one system. An AI agent answers support chats from your help center, calls your APIs via tools, workflows and MCP, and hands off when it should. Every chat, survey and vote is captured, deduplicated and scored by reach and revenue, so your roadmap runs on evidence, not opinions. Ship it and everyone who asked is notified. MCP for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Flat pricing, free plan.

projects.title: Habiv
projects.summary: Habiv is a home for games made with AI. Play for free in your browser with no download, climb daily leaderboards, remix what you like, and publish your own game straight from Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP-ready agent.

projects.title: AI Class by Kanary
projects.summary: Not a quiz. AI Class reads 30 days of your real Codex and Claude Code logs and turns them into one of 16 RPG classes: Knight, Ninja, Alchemist, Guild Master and 12 more. Six stats show how you actually work: volume, autonomy, chat length, context size, cache reuse and parallelism. Paste one prompt into your agent. It aggregates your logs locally and sends only totals. Conversations, prompts and project names never leave your machine. Free. No install. Your card in about a minute.

projects.title: Black Label Customer Tools
projects.summary: A read-only MCP connector for your Black Label account. List owned products, check remote-data readiness, get product guidance, search entitled lead and parcel services, and retrieve stored property audits from ChatGPT or Claude. Uses OAuth with PKCE and account-scoped entitlements. Requires an existing Black Label account; data searches require the matching product and active data credential. Local app files and controls stay on your machine.

projects.title: QQ
projects.summary: Run coding agents in your own workspace. QQ connects to your existing Codex subscription or supported model APIs, with a terminal UI, file editing, shell commands, MCP tools and visible activity. Download one open-source binary and start with a repository. We are adding JEV checkpoints to review tool results and task completion; that integration is in testing and is not yet included in v0.1.0.

projects.title: Mingle
projects.summary: Mingle is an open-source network where AI agents help their people find each other. Tell your agent who you want to meet, approve the exact card it publishes, and let other agents find relevant people. No profiles to browse, no feed, and no ranking people. Introductions are double opt-in, and contact details are released only after both sides choose to share. Works with Claude, Cursor, OpenClaw, and any MCP client.

projects.title: Show HN: Craigslist for agent skills, curated by a human
projects.author: skeptrune
projects.summary: hey, i'm nick (@skeptrune on X). i have been using ai for a lot of things i'm not an expert in and thought it would be nice to try and buy paid skills for helping it accomplish those tasks more efficiently. for example, redlining contracts, creating ai generated videos, different website designs, and more. curious to see if this resonates with folks here. i figure a more engineering'y audience that's ai coding-agent forward would have similar problems to what inspired me to make this

projects.title: Living Memory Lobby
projects.summary: Living Memory Lobby is the web entrance to Living Memory. Explore public rooms, start one with Empty, Work, or Dorm, or enter with a room link. Talk with the built-in guide, or connect your own AI through MCP. One link is enough — people without an AI harness can still walk in. Each room holds shared context and memories; return by URL. Browser visits let you explore without changing the room.

projects.title: LingYA Cosmos
projects.summary: Build a moonlit home, dress your avatar, and wander a tiny planet. LingYA Cosmos connects saved homes and outfits with a shared human-and-AI world, activity history, and a co-op puzzle. Built with Astra in Codex on an existing WebMCP prototype.

projects.title: Mantle
projects.summary: Mantle is an open-source service runtime and WebMCP-native Builder that turns business rules into typed schemas, views, procedures, and HTTP/MCP triggers. Design and verify a service in the browser, then hand it to a coding agent to materialize, verify, and deploy to your own Cloudflare account. The OSS, Builder, and first-class Cloudflare deployment path are live now. Mantle Cloud remains in Internal Beta with a waitlist.

projects.title: PetOS
projects.summary: Updated with GPT-6 Astra, PetOS is a local-first desktop duo for Windows and macOS that turns an animated companion into a useful layer for everyday work. Ask questions with text or images, open chat anywhere with a global shortcut, create reminders, run focus sessions, and keep context on-device. Connect Telegram and WeChat to continue from your phone. Link Codex and WorkBuddy to follow clear, human-readable agent progress instead of raw logs. No API key required.

projects.title: Graphrun
projects.summary: Model your system and APIs before you write code. Run journeys to see how requests, retries and failures behave, then implement with your favourite coding agent. Already have an app? Use the Graphrun skill and MCP to map it from code. Inspect components, export OpenAPI specs, and explore each step from request to result. This could help people understand a codebase, onboard new team members, and see how the different parts of an application work together.

projects.title: Codex Insights
projects.summary: $insights is a community Codex plugin that reports how you work from local sessions. Default is local-only: no model calls, credential redaction, and Trust & Coverage. Built with GPT-6 Astra. Inspired by Claude Code /insights.

projects.title: Fallow
projects.summary: Run npx fallow audit in any TypeScript or JavaScript repository. Fallow builds a deterministic dependency graph, then reports unused code, cycles, duplicated logic, complexity, and architecture drift. Its changed-code gate blocks only findings introduced by the current change, so existing debt does not stop adoption. Use the same evidence locally, in CI, editors, and MCP workflows. The analyzer is free and MIT licensed; optional Fallow Runtime adds production execution evidence.

projects.title: Noru Flow
projects.summary: Hands free: you never take the screenshot. Your agent asks over a local MCP server and gets one fresh capture plus the on-screen text, mid-task, without you cropping or pasting anything. Playwright already covers the DOM. Noru covers what it can't: native apps, simulators, system UI, final rendered pixels, and work spanning several apps. Nothing is uploaded. Captures stay on your Mac, Noru observes only, and every observation is acknowledged on screen first.

projects.title: AGENTCODI
projects.summary: AGENTCODI brings a native AI coding workspace to Android. It runs the Codex app-server locally, includes a real terminal and development toolchains, and adds its own protected sandbox with approval controls for commands and file access. No Termux, no WebView shell, no separate gateway. - Mcpasi/AGENTCODI

projects.title: VibeMatch
projects.summary: A decentralised AI social platform with a unique AI companion for everyone. Share and trade useful experience packs, engaging AI personalities and replicable agents through the Memory Store, helping creators earn. Voice and text AI share memories across devices.AI and app sandboxes let every user create a one-of-a-kind profile and social pet that reflect their personality, while real-time human–AI group chats, smart post editing, matchmaking and live status updates bring people together.

projects.title: OutlierKit
projects.summary: OutlierKit helps creators, businesses and agencies grow on YouTube. You enter one channel from your niche. Competitor Studio scans thousands of channels in that space and shows you who leads it, which titles and lengths earn the most views, which brands sponsor there, how those channels make money, and topics nobody has covered yet. Our MCP connector brings the same data into Claude, so you can just ask. The API serves it over REST. We use public YouTube data. You never connect your channel.

projects.title: Show HN: An agent-skill to generate preview, AppStore screenshots and campaigns

projects.summary: If you are developing apps and paying 3rd party services just to generate promotional visuals or app store screenshots - stop doing it I created an agent-skill which can do it for you with 3D device models (assets are CC-BY licensed) social cards/cover, app/play store screenshots, campaign 3d animating videos. projects.title: VPS Hosting Radar
projects.summary: Hosting pricing pages show the friendliest number. This is the other one: 19 plans, hand-collected, with what each costs once the advertised term ends — plus a four-question shortlist, a Chrome extension, and an open-source MCP. Free, CC BY 4.0.

projects.title: Tokenflow
projects.summary: Your AI coding agents bill you monthly and tell you nothing. TokenFlow reads the logs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Cline write on your machine, prices every branch, and posts the cost on the pull request as a comment plus a status check — so a change over its declared budget fails before it merges. A guard hook brakes a session while it is still running, and an MCP server hands the same numbers to the agent spending the money. Local-first, zero dependencies, MIT. Nothing leaves your machine.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】yovoice：简洁易用的本地 TTS 配音工具，支持音色复刻和情绪调节
projects.author: leemysw

projects.summary: 自荐一个本地 VS Code 扩展：ChatAnchor。 它解决的是 AI 编程里一个很常见、但挺烦人的小断点：项目文件夹改名或移动之后，Codex、Cursor Agent CLI、OpenCode 里的旧会话往往还停留在原路径，想继续原来的线程就要手动找记录、复制上下文，甚至重新解释一遍项目状态。 ChatAnchor 会给每个项目建立一个不随路径变化的本地身份，并结合 Git remote、commit、历史路径等线索，在目录位置变化后重新识别同一个项目。重新打开新目录后，可以直接在 VS Code 里继续原来的 Codex / Cursor / OpenCode 会话，或者从当前项目路径开启新的 agent 会话。 它还做了一点跨 agent 的上下文复用： Codex / Cursor 会话可以复制 @path，OpenCode 可以导出 JSON 或生成精简 Markdown transcript； 可以从最多 10 条已链接会话生成本地 Project Context Pack，再把这个 @path 交给另一个 agent； 默认扫描只读本地元数据，不读正文、不上传、不做遥测。只有显式执行导出、精简 transcript 或 Context Pack 时，才会读取用户选中的会话内容。 这个项目最初来自 Codex 官方 issue 26836 里讨论的问题：项目目录改名或移动后，原会话无法自动重新关联。我们也把 ChatAnchor 的方案整理成 comment 反馈给了 OpenAI 官方。

projects.title: Show HN: Nexus-Arc – pay-per-call and job escrow for AI agents on Arc
projects.author: irfndi
projects.summary: Hi HN — I built Nexus-Arc. AI agents can call APIs and run multi-step work, but they still cannot open a Stripe account or hold a corporate card. Prepaid credits lock capital; L1 fees make $0.001 calls uneconomic; L2 batch latency breaks tight loops. Nexus-Arc is a dual-rail gateway live on Arc mainnet (chain 5042), where USDC is native gas: 1. Synchronous rail — HTTP 402 / x402. Agent hits an endpoint unsigned, gets a 402 + challenge, signs a Permit2 / EIP-712 voucher, retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Settlement is in-process, sub-second, pay-per-call. No API keys. 2. Asynchronous rail — ERC-8183 escrow (NexusJobs). Client locks a USDC budget, provider submits a deliverable hash (IPFS/Arweave), evaluator releases payout. State machine: Open → Funded → Submitted → Terminal. Expiry refunds the client. Live screener (expect HTTP 402 on an unpaid GET): https://nexus-arc.pryx.dev/v1/screener Explorer: https://explorer.arc.io Stack is Bun + Effect TS on Arc. Fees are small (x402 ~0.1% + $0.0005; escrow 75 bps on completion). Happy to answer questions on the 402 self-facilitation path, Permit2 vouchers, or the escrow evaluator. What should I wire next — MCP tools, more paid APIs, or agent identity (ERC-8004)?

projects.title: [开源自荐] dsh-novel-craft：把作者的点选压成写作规律，只有规律进模型上下文
projects.author: shiyan688

github.name: shiyan688/dsh-novel-craft
github.description: 禁AI腔清单能让模型不像 AI，这个工作台让它像你：标好/坏段落 → 压成写作规律（只有规律进写稿上下文）→ 开新章（方向/候选/选段/合并定稿）→ 批注式微调（只改你标过的段，逐字核对）→ 张力曲线与账目体检。dsh 插件，775 条断言。

projects.summary: 安装：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-novel-craft（npm dsh-novel-craft@0.1.4，MIT） 这是什么 给中文网文/小说创作场景做的一个「作者品味校准」工作台，是 DeepSeek Harness 的插件（宿主半区 + 浏览器半区）。 一句话：一轮生成若干"结构不同"的候选稿，作者只做一件事——在觉得好的段落上点一下、在别扭的段落上点一下。这些点选被压成可复用的写作规律，下一轮写稿照着收敛。 我遇到的问题（自己写了半年小说，都是真事） 1. 禁AI腔清单能让模型不像 AI，但做不到"像这个作者"。 清单人人都在抄，抄完模型不油腻了，可它依然不是我。 2. 作者的真实反馈从来不沉淀。 今天说"太刻意"，明天说"没网感"，第三轮同一个毛病。因为我给的是评价，不是可复用的写法。 3. 原文喂不进上下文。 那把作者选中的段落整理成档案交给模型？起步 6 KB，一轮一个样，模型还得自己从原文里猜规律——猜不准，还烧掉上下文预算。 做法：三层分离，加一条硬规则 硬规则是：进模型上下文的只有规律，原文永远不进。 | 文件（都在 <候选目录>/.dsh-novel-craft/） | 给谁看 | 进上下文？ | | --- | --- | --- | | marks.json | 工作台（机器可读的好/坏标注） | ❌ 永不 | | 证据摘录.md | 原文证据，给人回查、给提炼当输入 | ❌（文件头写着"不要读进写稿上下文"） | | 作者偏好档案.md | 写稿会话只读这一份（只有规律） | ✅ 就它 | 真机数字（不是估算） 在一份真实书稿上点 30 段好/坏（第 1、2、8 章） 点一次「提炼规律」：1.8 秒回来 14 条规律 作者偏好档案.md 从 6140 B 的原文摘录变成 714 B 的规律，里面一条原文都没有 下一轮写稿只需要读这 714 B 提炼出来的规律长这样（原样抄几条）： 喜欢： 器物先动，人后发声，用声响顶点收束静默 给反派一句极短的私人恐惧，落点在赔不起 避免： 不要用比喻堆砌写人群的恐惧 不要用旁白解释反应者的心理活动 规律是怎么来的（以及为什么不是全自动） 一次便宜的辅助模型调用把待提炼的原文压成条目，但条目不直接进档案——作者逐条勾选才采纳，水位随之前移，同一段不会被重复送。规律区是作者的，工作台维护的自动块之外永不被覆盖，单条规律可以一键删掉。 顺手记两个插件坑（可能对写 dsh 插件的人有用） 1. 插件行的 apply 可能早于服务挂载：在 0.1.6-alpha.1 上实测，同步 apply 里 ctx.get('webServer') 拿到的是 undefined——写成"取不到就 return"的插件会在新版本上静默什么都不做。改成 ctx.inject(['settings','webServer'], …) 等就绪（带超时兜底）即可。 2. 调模型做结构化输出要默认关掉推理：推理 token 和正文共用一份输出预算，我这边表现是"接口 5.6 秒返回、解析出 0 条规律"，关掉推理 + 抬高预算后 1.8 秒出 14 条（官方 Discussion #6857 也写了这条）。 3. 另外客户端 bundle 的下发地址从 /plugins/<id>/client.js 变成了组合脚本 /plugins/??a/client.js,b/client.js&rev=…——插件不用管，但拿裸 URL 做测试的人会误以为"插件没被收录"。 工程质量 209 项断言：静态守卫（Hook 顺序、词条完整性）+ 回环端口上的接口闭环（含假 LLM 的提炼链路）+ 用成对 react/react-dom 把客户端组件真渲染成 HTML；测试不依赖任何本机路径 scripts/check-dsh-compat.mjs + CI 矩阵：每周自动在 latest / next / alpha / 0.1.2-rc.1 四档上真装一份 dsh、起服务、验宿主路由与客户端半区下发 出处与致谢：skills/novel-writing 的禁AI腔清单改编自 dsh-novel-solo（MIT），平台 DeepSeek Harness（MIT），完整声明在 THIRDPARTYNOTICES.md 仓库里还带了两个配套 skill（taste-calibration / novel-writing），装到 .dsh/skills/ 即可，插件负责"让你低负担地点"，skill 负责"告诉 agent 怎么用这些标注"。

projects.title: Show HN: Deiko – point at your screen, talk, and hand the brief to your agent
projects.author: maddy30445r
projects.summary: macOS, 0.4.5, free to try: curl -fsSL https://deiko.app/install.sh | sh I kept losing time explaining my own screen to Claude Code. Screenshot, crop, paste, then type three paragraphs describing which dropdown I meant. The context was all right in front of me and I was transcribing it by hand. Deiko: double-tap Right Option, and it listens while following your cursor. Hover what you mean while you talk — "this dropdown closes when I scroll, keep it open". Each thing you point at gets cropped and labelled. Tap Option to stop, and you get a brief plus the screenshots, which you drag into whatever agent you use. Works with two languages mixed in one sentence, which is how I actually talk. Screenshots and briefs never leave the Mac. Audio is transcribed then deleted; first 30 minutes use cloud transcription, after that it runs on-device forever. Things you should know before installing: - It's signed with a self-signed cert, not an Apple Developer ID, because I haven't paid the $99. That's why there's an install script: macOS quarantines the bundle, and the GUI "Open Anyway" misses the Node runtime nested inside, which then fails silently minutes later mid-transcription. The script is one `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` and a copy to /Applications. Read it first, it's short. - The bundle is ~110MB, mostly that Node runtime. - macOS 14+, Apple Silicon and Intel. - Pro ($3.99/mo) adds cloud transcription back and your own Sarvam/Groq key. Everything else is free and always will be. The thing I'm least sure about is whether pointing-while-talking actually beats just typing for people who aren't me. If you try it and it felt slower, I'd genuinely like to hear that.

projects.summary: I think the path Grok Bot took is absolutely the right one, the collaborating bots model is easy to understand and it maps to workflows naturally. However, Grok Bot is closed source and quite expensive (I ran out of tokens on Ultra tier), so I've decided to roll out my own: https://github.com/regnull/openbot . Same idea, you have collaborating bots that can be configured in any way you like. It supports all major LLM providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and local Ollama models. You can also configure model per bot - so you can have an engineer bot to work on most of the issues, and a senior engineer bot (using better, more expensive model) to tackle the most difficult ones. It's fully operational and at this point it pretty much improves itself - most of the PRs are authored by the bots themselves. I'm working on adding support for MCP servers, including OAuth, which would make it even more useful. Contributions are welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: Review agent changes locally before pushing
projects.author: GrinningFool
projects.summary: I've often found that agents do stupid things when implementing requests. When I only see their changes with limited context in a scroll-by approval blob, it's easy to miss some of that stupidity. In those cases, I'll often only see it when I can review the full change in context in a PR. This tool adds a local review step, giving the human a final opportunity to be in the loop: your agent commits the changes, pushes to a local 'review' remote, and waits for feedback. The push itself opens a review via post-receive hook, and provides you with a localhost URL to review the changes. If you request changes via inline comments (like you would for a PR), the agent sees the comments and makes adjustments. It pushes again and the process repeats until you're satisfied. When you approve the change, your agent can take whatever step is next in your normal workflow - push to open an actual PR, merge locally, etc. These are lightweight instructions (~500 tokens) that should be customized for your workflow.

projects.title: [开源自荐] tool-bridge: Agent 的触手, 连接 设备/Context/MCP. 支持反向注册, SDK...
projects.author: Disdjj
projects.summary: 先上链接: 官方文档: 过去一年在一些AI Starup 工作, 在这些强调 AI Native 的公司中做 Agent Infra 的过程中, 经常会遇到一些问题: 1. 大量的不同业务的 Agent 希望能够共享工具, 但是也希望有足够的限制(某些工具禁止访问) 2. 希望 Agent 和 Agent 之间能够共享 Context, 用飞书cli 太重, 而且 agent 创建的文档访问权限控制很麻烦 3. 聚合MCP, 提供统一的开发体验, 某些 MCP 由于 Seat 限制不能够添加过多的 User 席位, 而且最好能够自部署, 没有商业风险 4. 希望能够直接让 Agent 使用某些命令排查线上的机器/Pod/服务 5. 自建的 mcp 又总是很难注册到 MCP Gateway 以上就是我在做 Agent Infra 遇到的一些问题, 分散来看, 每一个其实都有解决方案. 比如说 mcporter / mintlify / 各种 mcp gateway / agentdock ... 但是作为部署/管理/成本/维护的考虑, 把这些功能分散到 N 个服务中好像有太过于舍本逐末. 于是最近两个月, 我做了 tool-bridge, 简单来说: 基于树描述组织中的所有工具/MCP/Context/设备, 提供类似 cli 的 help 语义 + agent自主的 feedback + SDK + 支持反向注册, 实现的一套 Agent 的工具调用方式. 当然, 本身是兼容 MCP 的, 同时 tool-bridge 也支持 接入mcp, 也支持以 mcp 的方式暴露. 几个用例 目前的范围能力 tool-bridge 对开发者提供: SDK / Plugin-SDK / 完全开源的 Server / Dashboard tool-bridge 对Agent提供: API / CLI / MCP 的接入支持 tool-bridge 对设备提供: 1. linux / mac / windows 的 shell / Daemon / 自定义设备路径 的能力 2. ios / android 的通知/可离线投递的信箱/震动/闪光/摄像头调用(根据设置权限) 的能力 目前我把目前使用的 Agent 对 MCP/Context/设备 的调用都迁移到了 tool-bridge, 体验不错, 推荐使用! 欢迎 Star/Issue/PR, 目前处于 Pre-Launch 的阶段, API UI CMD 可能会有变更, 但是会尽快推出 1.0 的 Stable-Release

projects.title: Show HN: Blue – open-source governance for coding agents
projects.author: tomislavs
projects.summary: Hey HN, After migrating to an inference gateway to serve internal usage across an organization, problems have started to pop up. Once you detach from a managed ecosystem such as OpenAI or Anthropic you lose governance capabilities that makes the transition difficult. - Losing access to a central plugin hub for delivering MCPs, skills, etc. A gateway can sort of do this but has low compatibility beyond skills, different harnesses, and version ranges - Inability to deliver managed config (model defaults, etc). Can sort of be done with MDM/Jamf but doesn't reach contractors and doesn't follow employees to other machines - Gateway configuration is awkward for devs transitioning from SSO and API keys sit in plain text on their machines The gateway transition facilitates new model families (Kimi, Deepseek, etc) which are best utilized with new harnesses beyond Codex or Claude Code. Managing these additional tools multiplies the governance problems. Lastly, attempting to deliver an attribution program which can tag inference requests with ticket numbers and other metadata to facilitate Opex/Capex calcs for finance becomes fairly unfeasible when there are multiple harnesses across arbitrary versions. This was not solved with managed ecosystems either to be fair, but requires some self-serve program or some local MITM proxy which is a distribution and versioning problem in of itself. I built Blue to attempt to solve these problems. It's an MIT open source, self-hostable control plane. Developers install a universal CLI and point it at their hosted control plane tenant. On launch, it reconciles the organization's policy per harness, delivers extensions, and configures the gateway. It then launches and passes control to the native CLI (Kimi, OpenCode, Codex, etc) that devs already use. Authentication is via browser device authorization which mints ephemeral bearer tokens. For gateway access, these tokens are exchanged at the inference proxy (part of the self-hosted Blue image) for the real API keys. This means that devs don't need to manage API keys or even log into the gateway at all. Lastly, SCIM and OIDC are supported out of the box, so orgs can connect their identity solution immediately. Curious to hear your thoughts and if you have/solved this problem. I believe it can also be solved to some degree with a harness like Pi or even OpenCode, but that of course depends on the entire org migrating to those. Last thing I'll say is nowadays a CLI isn't enough since I've seen over 80% of devs prefer desktop apps like the ChatGPT app. We're also working on an open source desktop app that supports metaharnesses like Blue to make this transition easier. Thanks!

projects.title: 我们做了一门让 Agent 写视频的语言
projects.author: Daniel6606
projects.summary: 大家好啊，最近我们在做 Hypit： 这是一个视频描述语言，我们起名叫 SVML （ Semantic Video Markup Language ） 我们希望 Claude Code 、Codex 这样的 Agent ，能用它描述一支视频，再交给系统生成素材、处理字幕、编排画面，最后渲染成片。 项目链接： https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit ## 从一个很具体的剪辑问题开始 我们之前给一些 AI 公司做内容，经常会参考别人做得不错的广告，再结合自己的产品重新制作 一条二十几秒的视频，要拆脚本、生成镜头、配音、剪辑、加字幕，还要安排产品特写和各种动效。即使模型已经把素材生成出来，后面依然有不少制作工作，如果你做过这件事情，你一定会知道我在说什么 其中有一件事一直让我们觉得很绕啊 写脚本的时候，我经常会边写边在脑子里构思稿子和视频的配合，比如： > 主持人说到产品名，就弹出产品卡片 > 说到“第一名”，排行榜对应的位置就亮起来 但此时还不知道这些词会落在第几秒，于是只能等语音和视频生成完，再一帧一帧地找位置，把效果对上 如果换一版台词或者只是语速变了，就得重新处理这些对应关系 所以我们想让 Agent 能直接写下这种要求，由系统根据实际素材算出时间，这个想法后来成了 SVML 里很核心的一部分：把画面效果绑定到叙事中的词 ## 视频的源文件可以长什么样 下面是一段真实的.svml 语言+视频的 demo ![]( https://i.imgur.com/AMCcmgR.gif) 把 GIF 中的案例简化 ⬇️ ``` 我会把它加进 @lifestyle 咖啡、奶昔，甚至煮意面的水里。 你这是把它当 @/lifestyle 面粉用了吧。 ``` daily-creatine 是段落名称，GIRL 和 GUY 标明每句话由谁说。 @lifestyle 和 @/lifestyle 划出了一段跨越两位说话人的语义区间。补充画面可以绑定到这段区间，覆盖相应的对话。 实际案例中的画面组件，就是通过 during={story.selection.lifestyle} 引用这段范围。 (查看完整播客源码: https://github.com/hypit-ai/hypit/blob/main/examples/podcast/reference.svml) 这些标记本身只描述位置，具体显示什么，由引用它们的组件决定。素材生成后，系统通过语音对齐，把这些位置映射到实际时间。改台词或换语言时，重新生成、对齐相关素材，画面就能按新的时间定位。 完整的语法说明在： https://hypit.ai/quickstart/script/ ## 复刻视频，是这门语言的一个入口 现在最容易体验 Hypit 的方式，是给 Agent 一条参考视频，让它把里面的画面、台词、字幕和特效关系重建成 workflow ![]( https://i.imgur.com/rNe3HKa.gif) 可以看这个街头采访的案例：同一套结构，可以把主持人换成，被采访者换成动漫人物，F1 赛车手等 做出第一个版本后，源文件可以继续改: 换产品、换开场、换语言，批量生成 100 个变体，都可以围绕已有流程来做；需要重新生成的素材仍然会产生相应成本 当然，也可以没有参考视频。直接描述要做什么，由 Agent 从零组织组件和编写源文件。字幕、动效和代码渲染画面这类流程，也可以不调用生成模型。 ## 怎么用 Hypit 给 Claude Code ，Codex ，或者 Hermes 安装 skills 先： ``` npx skills add hypit-ai/hypit -g ``` 然后提供一条参考视频： ``` /hypit 复刻这个视频: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` 首次使用时，Agent 会检查并协助准备运行环境。你可以继续告诉它要改什么，检查制作方案、确认所需服务和费用，再生成成片。上手文档 Hypit 本身免费，不收席位费和按次渲染费；付费模型 API 和 Agent 的费用另算，平均制作一个视频的 API 成本，换算下来在 1 美金左右！ 欢迎大家来提提建议

projects.summary: llmdoc首页: 标题的说明 标题的实践考验指的是在两个 AI Starup 公司的实践, 支撑了大约 3 亿 ARR 产品的迭代(其实应该是 2.9 亿 ARR, 四舍五入其实差不多, 当然了其实是两家公司的两家产品加起来的 ARR 😭) 在前司主要负责公司的 AI/Agent 建设, 同时也比较深入的参与了业务的开发, 一些开发上的尤其是 人&人, 人&AI 的协作的痛点感知还是非常清晰的. 我相信我列出的问题肯定不止一个人遇到过: 1. AI 写的代码没有沿用默认的技术框架/方案 2. 需要在 Coding 前不断地输入/纠正 3. 已经有的解决方案/函数/包库没有直接用, 又造了一堆轮子 4. 明明纠正过很多次, 同样的错误在下一次又犯病 5. 使用的 memory 没有版本化管理, 代码回滚/合并了, memory 没有更新 6. 给了目标之后, 用了巨多时间巨多 context, 读取了N 多文件, 问了 N 个问题, 然后在过了甜点 context 阈值的情况下开始工作, 写的乱七八糟 context floor 我曾经给很多人表达过一个观点: Agent 完成工作的好坏, 取决于 context 的丰富程度 这里有几个需要说明的地方: 1. 工作的好坏: 这里是靠人判断的, 架构是否合理, 抽象是否清晰, 是不是没有重复造轮子... 2. Context 的丰富程度: 这里指的是和"完成目标"相关的 Context, 尽可能的多而且不重复, 在 context 无限大, 甜点 window 无限长的情况下, 最好的方案是把代码库+架构+db+UI+PRD 全都塞进去 换句话说: 如果有办法能够稳定的为 Agent 提供良好的快速到达满足工作条件的 Context 路径, 就能提升 Agent 的工作效果和工作效率 context floor 只是我臆造的一个名词, 大家不用搜索, 我在一篇早期的 blog 里简单的说了一下, 大家不用关心 llmdoc 好了, 为了引出正文已经瞎扯了很多了

projects.summary: 之前在 V2EX 发过几次 free4.chat ，最早就是一个不用注册、打开链接就能聊的 WebRTC 语音聊天室。 上次更新还是给房间里塞了一个 AI 助手。最近又折腾了不少，现在方向有点不一样了：不再自己托管一个 AI Bot ，而是让你本来就在用的 Agent 直接进房间。 目前 Codex 、Claude 、Pi 、Hermes 、OpenCode 这些都可以作为独立参与者加入。 比如我现在实际跑过的场景： Mac mini 上跑一个 Agent ，MacBook 上跑另一个 Agent 。两个 Agent 加入同一个临时房间，可以互相发现、发任务请求、接受或拒绝，然后把文件和结果通过房间传回来。 不需要共享文件系统，也不需要把两个 Agent 放进同一个平台。 人也可以直接在浏览器房间里和 Agent 协作。现在有 Task ，可以单独和某个 Agent 干一件事，发图片/文件，看执行状态； Agent 需要权限时可以在房间里弹审批卡；如果纯文字不太好表达，Agent 还可以临时生成一个简单的交互界面。 Agent 自己的模型、工具、代码仓库、浏览器登录状态、API Key 都还是留在自己的机器上，free4chat 只负责提供一个临时房间把它们连起来。 浏览器不是必须的，两个 Agent 也可以直接从终端建房、加入然后协作。 在线： https://free4.chat/ 开源： https://github.com/i365dev/free4chat Agent 协作文档： https://www.free4.chat/docs/guides/cross-machine-collaboration 之前的帖子： https://v2ex.com/t/828646 https://v2ex.com/t/1213306 最近基本把这个项目当 Agent 协作的实验田了，如果有人平时同时用 Codex / Claude / Pi 之类的，可以试试看这种“临时拉进一个房间干活”的方式有没有实际用途。

projects.title: Show HN: Agentbox – Teleport your repo into sandboxes with no worktree juggling
projects.author: madarco
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Marco, I've built this MIT-licensed CLI command to parallelize my work with claude / codex / PI, because with worktrees I had ports conflicts, agents conflicting for browser use, or touching external files. It copies your project, skills, subscription oauth, and can optionally carry external files, supports LFS, and adds Chrome and screensharing via webVNC, so I use it for Godot game for eg. To use: agentbox claude # launch on docker, also with pi, codex, opencode and: agentbox hetzner claude # also digitalocean, e2b, vercel, daytona, islo, Sprites, Tenki or your own private cloud: agentbox remote-docker add buildbox marco@10.0.0.9 agentbox docker:buildbox claude Most importantly your git credentials / gh tokens are not copied into the sandboxes, but changes are relayed through your pc, with shims for git, gh or any CLI from your host, with your approval. I use it to drive multiple subagents from a "Firstmate" agent: I request several changes or gives him a backlog of items and claude will splits them in groups into parallel cloud sandboxes to avoid conflicts, and drive the sessions with the special "agentbox drive" commands, for eg. to wait-for idle, plan-approval, questions etc. I find it really usefull so far, since it allows me to keep using my existing IDE/tools. More info on https://github.com/madarco/agentbox

projects.title: Show HN: Plurnk (Yet *Another* AI Harness)
projects.author: wikitopian
projects.summary: I am desperate for feedback on my homebrewed harness, "Plurnk." I've been dogfooding it on my RTX5070Ti with only 16GB VRAM as my daily driver for weeks now and it's genuinely better than everything else available (I'm biased). 1. Curation, not Compaction The model's fully responsible (bitter lesson) for deterministically curating its own context. 2. ANTLR Grammar The dozen verbs for the harness are optimized for model pretraining, looking like markdown while being fully integrated with an EBNF grammar that plugs into an AST for superior workflow and recovery. 3. Universal Resources Everything's addressable by the model through a pseudo-URI interface, including the log entries. 4. Omnipatterns Everything in the repo goes through treesitters which build a complete graph that the model can search with glob, regex, jsonpath, xpath, graph, and sqlite fulltext. 5. Standards MCP2 tools, AG-UI client interface, A2A "agent to agent", plugs into everything through OAI spec + models.dev 6. Interfaces CLI, TUI, and a Neovim plugin, easy to extend, very pluggable 7. Lean Agent Service/Client architecture with lean TUI allows dozens of agents to run on weak hardware. 200MB footprint. 8. Lean Context Achieves all of the "batteries includes" features of a fat harness while the sysprompt is only slightly larger than pi agent's. It started as a proof of concept for my bespoke opinions on what "bitter lesson" actually means, and it's gone so well that I believe others trying to build agentic workflows, especially with local and humble constraints, could benefit from the proven concepts.

projects.title: Show HN: Omni – Open-source workplace agent, built on Postgres
projects.author: prvnsmpth
projects.summary: Hi HN! Over the past year, I've been building Omni ( https://github.com/getomnico/omni ) - an open-source, self-hosted agent that connects to your workplace apps (drive, email, wiki, CRMs, ticketing systems, etc.), and gives your team an AI agent that can operate across these apps. I posted about Omni on HN about 6 months ago, and it generated some interesting discussions: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47215427 . At the time, Omni was largely an enterprise search system. Since then, the project has evolved to become more of an agent that can gather context, analyze information, and carry out tasks; rather than just search for answers. E.g., you can tell Omni, "create a project status deck on Google Slides with this week's progress", and it will search through Jira, Slack, Docs, meeting transcripts, fetch the relevant information, analyze spreadsheets with Python, prepare a summary and ask for your approval before creating the slides on your drive. A non-exhaustive list of things Omni can do today: - Take action on connected apps, with an approval system for write actions - Full MCP support, so connectors can integrate with any existing MCP servers. - Sync data from connected apps into a unified search index, allowing the agent to query data across all apps using a single search tool. - Sand-boxed code execution and shell access, enabling the agent to create documents, spreadsheets, presentations and HTML landing pages. - Persistent memory and user-defined skills Omni still uses Postgres as its core data layer where it syncs and indexes all data from connected apps. We use ParadeDB (Postgres extension) for BM25 search and pgvector for semantic search - so there's no need to run and operate a dedicated search cluster or vector database. To know more about the architecture: https://docs.getomni.co/architecture . Would love to get more folks involved in the project, so if you find this interesting, please check out the repo below. It only takes around 10-15 min to deploy using docker compose and connect a few apps. Happy to answer any questions! GitHub: https://github.com/getomnico/omni (Apache 2.0 licensed) Docs: https://docs.getomni.co

projects.author: mack-peng

github.description: css graph for AI Agent

projects.summary: 我是 cssgraph 的作者，自荐这个 MIT 协议的开源项目（还有一个姊妹项目 cssprobe-cli）。 cssgraph 解决一个很具体的问题：AI 编程助手（Claude Code / Cursor / Codex 等）想搞清楚「这个 className 的样式从哪儿来、被谁覆盖、影响哪些文件」时，只能靠 grep + 逐文件 Read，一次次手工重建级联，既慢又费 token。 cssgraph 把项目的样式表（CSS / SCSS / Less / Sass / PostCSS、CSS-in-JS、CSS Modules、Tailwind v3/v4）解析成一个本地 SQLite 知识图谱，通过 MCP 暴露 13 个工具——一次工具调用就能拿到某个 className 的属性、覆盖关系、特异性、引用它的组件与影响范围（O(1) 精确查找）。100% 本地运行，支持自动增量同步，索引不会过期。 快速开始 bash npm i -g cssgraph cd your-project && cssgraph init cssgraph mcp-install # 自动配置 Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / opencode / Gemini CLI 等 姊妹项目 cssprobe-cli 运行时 CSS 探针（基于 Playwright）：回答「为什么这个元素溢出、滚动链在哪、containing block 被谁劫持」这类静态代码看不出来的问题，给 AI 一份真实渲染现场 + ASCII 布局图。两者一静一动，合起来是完整的 CSS 诊断链路。

projects.title: Show HN: Agenttik – work on multiple projects in parallel with AI agents
projects.author: psanchez
projects.summary: Hi! I've been reading HN daily for almost 16 years. Really glad this community exist. This is my first Show HN, so I hope you find this tool useful/interesting. During my summer holidays I started playing with latest AI models on personal projects. At one point I started working in parallel with the same project and tried different approaches. The one that worked best for me was to clone the repo and distribute work among different AI workers, work in parallel but with different branches & folders. This allowed me to review and merge work afterwards. The thing is, spawning several agents in parallel was challenging. I could work on multiple features and bugfix at once, but it was hard to keep track what I was working on. I was jumping from one thing to another, and back; from one window to another. Switching tasks like this was mentally exhausting. Holidays were over, and after returning to my day to day work, I continued working using a similar approach not on one, but also on multiple projects, but I still could not find how to work in a more organized way without the mental toll. This space is growing really fast, and I haven't been able to find the right tool for myself, so I decided to build my own. I wanted a tool that would help me manage multiple projects at once, work with multiple agents, even from different providers, where I could chose between my personal and work subscriptions depending on the project, where I could easily review changes without leaving the tool if I wanted, or go all in and delegate fully to agents; one where I had quick shortcuts to move around, where I could schedule work or enqueue work for later so agents could work on one task after another. agenttik is my way of tackling this problem to work on multiple projects in parallel, while allowing myself to be on the driver seat. I can give as much autonomy as I want to the agents while keeping things organized in my head. I've been hesitating for hours on whether to submit or not, but hey "if you are not ashamed of your project, you are shipping too late" Honestly, this project has exactly one week of development, started from scratch, and even though it is still early on, it has been extremely useful for me. I've built in a week things that would have taken me months, not only built the tool itself but other projects as well (most of the merit is still on the models used, but would have had no way of distributing all the work, though). Feel free to try. Here's how I would get started: - Open a project you already have - Add some general prompt (in the project area) or add to your AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (to instruct it to do regular commits and/or work with branches, and also instructions on how to build effective tests so that it can self-correct). - Chose your subscriptin of choice: Claude Code / Open AI subscription / ... - Pick big models (Opus High to Max / Fable Medium to Max / Astra Medium to Max) for bigger autonomy and try not to do hand-holding Finally, start sending/enqueuing tasks on all the features you want your product to have, bugfixes, ... use a new prompt per task (Ctrl+T / Cmd+T), I recommend using big models to avoid investing your own time reviewing, and then once LLM is done, review and archive that task or continue iterating. Keep adding tasks as you think on them. Add more projects as you start feeling comfortable. It has been really addictive for me to see the speed of development when working like this. I got totally hooked. Speed of iteration is insane. Happy to discuss any feedback you have even if it is about other tools or ways of working with AI these days! I hope you like it!!

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Flashgate：让 AI 编程 agent 不敢谎报固件能跑的硬件验证门禁
projects.author: Lion-1209

github.name: Lion-1209/flashgate
github.description: The agent can't claim the firmware works — until the board says so. Hardware-in-the-loop verification gate: build → flash → boot banner → exit code.

projects.summary: 我是 Flashgate 的维护者，自荐这个 MIT 开源的硬件在环验证工具。 AI 编程 agent 改完固件经常直接宣布"能跑了"——但它其实无从知道板子上的真实情况，编译通过不等于板子能启动。Flashgate 把最后一环交给硬件裁决： 完整验证链：编译 → ST-Link/OpenOCD 烧录 → 等板子自报身份（串口 banner 带 git sha，或 64 字节 SWD RAM 签名，后者不需要串口线）→ 发真实控制台命令、断言硬件寄存器读回值 → 结构化退出码 Stop hook 门禁：挂进 Claude Code 后，agent 改了固件没过真机验证就想收工，会被当场拦下，并把板子的失败证词（比如"收到呼吸灯命令却回报 OFF"）喂回给 agent 定位修复 每次验证（无论成败）落一份可审计的证据记录：逐项检查结论、板子原话、产物哈希 bench-serve 可把整台实验台挂上局域网，远程 agent 通过 Arm 的 device-connect 协议发现并请求真机验证（跨机实测通过） 自带 OpenOCD 后端，不需要 ST 工具链；仓库含完整可编译的 STM32H743 示例工程（正点原子 Apollo），接线后开箱可跑 仓库里有一段完整的真实 agent 会话记录：agent 被板子拦下、读证词、定位到固件里一处"静默无操作谎言"、修复、真机通过后才放行。 Python 编写，pip install flashgate 即用，目前以 STM32 为主（适配器层本周已落地，欢迎其他芯片的档案贡献）。

Query conversations and dates from AI coding tools, reuse matching messages, and fill missing attachments from later exports. MIT licensed. Highlights Maintainer self-submission. This is an early release with a downloadable Apple Silicon Mac app, Chinese-first documentation, English documentation, synthetic fixtures, and CI. Receives WeChat's native shared ZIPs through a Swift macOS share extension. Users choose a local conversation name instead of relying on unavailable native group IDs. The Python CLI uses the standard library and returns JSON, context and local attachment paths. It can be used by existing Codex, Claude Code or other agent sessions with shell access. Separates canonical messages from import provenance. A later export can supply a missing video without adding another copy of the matched message. Original files remain available for verification. Useful as a small example of connecting a native sharing extension, file receipts, SQLite and an agent-friendly CLI. Current scope: Apple Silicon Mac; Python 3.9+ for the CLI. Same-minute identical messages exported separately can be ambiguous because matching is not based on WeChat message IDs. ChatDrop itself does not upload chats; external AI tools have their own data handling. I checked the repository URL in the HelloGitHub website search and searched existing GitHub submissions before submitting; no matching result was visible. Example Code bash chatdrop conversations chatdrop search --conversation 'Product group' --from 2026-09-01 --to 2026-09-16 --all chatdrop context '<message-id>' --radius 3 Screenshots or Demo Videos Real native app AI-generated sharing illustration with fictional conversation names: Download and setup:

projects.author: max1874

github.name: max1874/ferry
github.description: Self-hosted clipboard and file ferry for devices on one private network: a single Go server with a built-in web app, so any browser is a client. Native iOS and Android apps are optional.

projects.summary: 协议：Apache-2.0 ｜ 版本：v1.0.0，Docker 镜像支持 amd64 / arm64 一句话 不用读部署文档。把 README 顶部那段话复制给 Claude Code、Codex 这类能在电脑上执行命令的 agent，它会用 Docker 把 Ferry 部署好，然后带你用手机扫码接入，完成第一次文字和文件传输。 部署：交给 agent README 第一节就是一段可以直接复制的提示词（中文版）。里面写清楚了 agent 需要做什么，也写清楚了哪些事不能做： 读 README 和最新 Release，使用发布好的 Compose 部署包和对应镜像，不从源码临时构建； 检查系统、CPU 架构、Docker 和 Compose；缺依赖时先说明并征得你同意，已有部署先备份再升级； 选私有局域网 IP、检查端口，多个网络拿不准时先问你；不暴露到公网，不关防火墙； 部署完检查容器、日志和局域网 HTTP 访问，告诉你访问地址，以及启停、升级、备份的命令； 引导你进入 Devices → Connect another device 扫码，并区分它自己验证过的和仍需要你拿手机确认的，不会把本机检查通过说成跨设备传输成功。 想自己动手的话，README 里也有常规的快速开始，下载 Compose 包，docker compose up -d 即可。 Ferry 是什么 一个自托管的剪贴板与文件摆渡工具，长得像聊天：所有设备共用一条时间线，手机上发的链接、电脑上的截图、一段命令，在另一台设备上点一下就能复制或下载。 设备只需要浏览器。 手机、平板、电脑打开地址就能加入，什么都不用装。 内容不出你的网络。 一个 Go 进程，消息存在 SQLite 里，文件原样保存（单个最大 64 MB，不重新编码）；没有账号、遥测和第三方服务。 是时间线，不是一次性传输。 标注来自哪台设备，明天还能翻到。 剪贴板归你自己。 只在你按粘贴快捷键或点复制按钮时读写，从不在后台读取。 和"给自己发微信"比，内容不经过别人的服务器，截图也不被压缩；和 AirDrop 比，不限苹果设备，而且有可以回翻的历史。 边界 为可信的家庭或办公室私有网络设计，默认是 HTTP，不支持直接暴露到公网；需要 HTTPS 可以自己在内网加一层 Caddy 等反向代理。 iOS 和 Android 原生 App 在仓库里，但不属于 1.0.0 的发布内容，日常使用浏览器即可。 我是作者，自荐。不合适直接关掉即可。

projects.summary: termcp 是一个支持可视化管理的面向 AI Agent 的通用交互式终端 MCP。 现在的 Agent 很擅长执行 ls、git status、curl 这类「运行一次就结束」的命令，但遇到真正的交互式程序就比较麻烦： SSH 可能先询问密码，安装程序会在中途弹出 [Y/n]，Python REPL 需要逐行输入，vim、gdb、htop、数据库 CLI 则从头到尾都在等待下一次键盘操作。 这些程序不是一次 exec 能完成的。 termcp 的思路不是为 vim 做一个 MCP、为 gdb 再做一个 MCP、为某个数据库 CLI 再做一个 MCP，而是直接把完整的终端交互能力提供给 Agent。 只要一个工具原本能够在终端里使用，Agent 就可以尝试直接通过 termcp 操作它： Agent → MCP → termcp → PTY → 任意 CLI 因此，大量已经存在几十年的命令行工具，不需要为了 AI 再重新包装一遍 API 或 MCP Server。 特点 1. 真正的交互式终端 termcp 底层使用真实 PTY。 Agent 可以读取终端输出、向 stdin 输入文本，也可以发送 Enter、Tab、Esc、Ctrl+C 等按键，然后继续读取新的输出。 也就是说，它可以像人一样不断执行： 观察 → 判断 → 输入 → 再观察 vim、gdb、htop、Python REPL、交互式安装器等程序都可以直接运行，而不是退化成一连串 bash -c。 2. Shell 会话可以跨多轮对话持续存在 Agent 启动一个程序后，不需要这一轮对话结束时把它关掉。 同一个 Shell 可以一直存在，下一轮继续操作；一条连接上还能同时打开多个 Shell，例如一个终端跑程序，另一个终端查看日志。 终端输出使用游标增量读取，不会每次都把整个历史重新塞进模型上下文。 3. 本机和远程服务器使用同一套接口 termcp 把所有终端统一成 SSH。 远程机器使用正常 SSH；本机则通过进程内嵌的 SSH Server 建立内存连接，不额外监听 TCP 端口。 因此对于 Agent 来说，本机和远程服务器没有区别。 文件操作使用 SFTP，同时支持 SSH 的本地、远程和动态端口转发。 4. 人可以实时观察并随时接管 termcp 自带 Web UI。 运行后打开： 就可以看到 Agent 正在操作的同一个终端。 vim、htop 等动态界面也会正常显示，多个终端可以像 iTerm2 一样平铺。 如果 Agent 操作错了，人可以随时直接接管键盘继续输入。 会话结束后，终端历史仍然会被保存，重启 termcp 后也可以继续查看。 5. SSH 凭据不需要交给模型 SSH 密码和私钥由 termcp 本地管理，写入后无法通过 MCP 再读取。 Agent 只需要知道一个配置名称，例如： prod-web 然后请求「连接 prod-web」即可。 主机地址、用户名、端口、密码和私钥都不需要出现在模型上下文里。 Agent 修改 SSH 配置的能力默认也是关闭的。 快捷部署 一个二进制即可运行 termcp 使用 Go 编写，MIT 协议，提供 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的预编译版本。 Web UI、MCP SSE 和 Streamable HTTP 共用一个端口，默认是 18765，数据保存在本地 ~/.termcp，不需要额外数据库。 Claude Code、Open WebUI 以及其他支持 MCP 的客户端都可以接入。 我们希望 termcp 做的不是「再给一个工具开发一个 MCP」，而是给 Agent 一双能够操作终端的手。 只要一个工具能在终端里运行，它就有机会直接成为 Agent 的工具。

projects.title: Show HN: Rebuno - An open-source runtime for production agents
projects.author: nnww
projects.summary: I have been building Rebuno, an open-source execution runtime for operating AI agents in production. It manages execution state and guardrails across agents built with different frameworks. Agents run as HTTP services. Rebuno dispatches work through signed webhooks and keeps execution state in Postgres. Agents submit tool and model calls to Rebuno as steps before executing them. For each new step, Rebuno evaluates per-agent YAML policies, independently of the model's prompt. It can allow the call, deny it, or hold it for human approval. The agent executes permitted calls and reports their outcomes. Policy decisions and step outcomes are both recorded in one append-only event log. After an interruption, the agent starts its handler from the top. Steps with recorded outcomes return those outcomes instead of executing again. A crash can also leave a tool with no recorded outcome. Tools marked safe_to_retry run again, and tools marked at_most_once fail as indeterminate. How the agent handles an indeterminate step is up to its implementation. There are Python and TypeScript SDKs, and the repo includes examples using LangChain, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, Vercel AI SDK, and Mastra. Rebuno is free to self-host and released under the MIT licensed. I'd be interested in hearing how others are running or operating agents in production. Blog post with diagrams: https://rebuno.io/blog/introducing-rebuno Getting started: https://docs.rebuno.io/getting-started

projects.title: Show HN: Slowave – local adaptive memory for coding agents
projects.author: mrsalty
projects.summary: I started building Slowave because I kept running into the same problem with coding agents: every new session has the codebase and some documentation but not the context behind it, decisions that brought you there and especially the thinking process behind the code. Most memory system solutions focus primarily on the storage and retrieval aspects (vector search/RAG/graphs/ Markdown files, etc.). After months of storing memories (coding 8+ hours a day produces a lot of memories) these might hallucinate your reasoning model and they can clutter your context window. To treat semantic relationship, such as contradiction, supersession, etc, most systems added an extra LLM layer that summarize memories and continuously evaluate their semantic relevance. That comes with a non-negligible cost and introduces a split-brain system, where a second model is making decisions about memory independently of the agent actually using it. I started looking up into how human brain works, and the first thing striking me was that retrieval is just a part of the whole memory problem. Brain memories are a constant flow of information where what matters gets reinforced, what doesn't decays over time. What really matters for an efficient memory system is to retrieve memories that actually help (a human or an agent) to achieve its current task or goal given the current context. Everything else should be treated as noise. Slowave is my attempt to approach this problem differently: It instructs your coding agent to participate in maintaining its own memory. Each task becomes a feedback loop between your agent and the memory layer: remember -> recall -> use -> feedback -> reinforce / weaken -> decay Your agent tells Slowave whether retrieved memories were useful, irrelevant or stale. Slowave uses that signal to adapt those memories salience. Retrieval works upon this continuous loop of feedback, reinforcement or decay. This means Slowave doesn't need a separate LLM or LLM judge for memory maintenance. The agent is already evaluating what helped; Slowave handles the mechanical part of adapting the memory substrate. Slowave runs fully locally. It uses a lightweight multilingual embedding model and SQLite, with no external memory service or LLM API required. It works with only 5 MCP endpoints. It currently supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, OpenCode, Windsurf and Claude Desktop. With the local dashboard you can inspect (and delete) your memories, procedures, retrievals and see metrics to measure how it's being valuable for your agent(s). Slowave is still in public beta but I'd be grateful to receive any feedback both on the approach and, if you try it, on how it works for you.

projects.title: Show HN: GSL – I wanted to describe the architecture, not just draw it
projects.author: dnnrly
projects.summary: I built GSL because I got fed up of building architecture diagrams that couldn't quite capture all of the nuance of the real world. I liked the idea of using a system like Mermaid or PlantUML to represent my systems but there was never really a satisfactory way of describing what was happening. I liked the easy-to-follow syntax of those diagramming tools but they very quickly ran into limitations. When you describe an API gateway component, you can't really say that it belongs in a specific region but also that it belonged in a certain zone of the architecture or which team owns it. And when I described what systems interacted with each other I only had the ability to use a text field to describe all of the metadata about the relationship. Is it HTTPS vs an async lambda invocation? What auth do we need? Something else I wanted was the ability to query the architecture. Surely when you have the full graph of what talks to what, you should be able to pose questions like: * "which customer actions trigger a call to vendor X's API?" * "what will be affected if database Y goes down?" I couldn't really find anything that did that in a way that felt natural. Diagramming tools were either completely visual or too presentation focussed to express what I wanted. Existing graph languages felt too clunky or cumbersome. I struggled to find any that worked with sets and querying in a way that felt right. So one rainy afternoon, I decided to see how far I could get with ChatGPT and some ideas - GSL was born! In the repo there is: * A specification for GSL, a language for defining directed graphs with nodes and edges along with set annotations to declare cross-cutting relationships * A specification for GQL, the companion query language * gsl-query - a CLI tool for executing queries on your GSL models * gsl-diagram - a very primitive tool for turning GSL into Mermaid or PlantUML diagrams * A small VS Code plugin for syntax highlighting * Guides, tutorials, documentation * Rich examples (including some non-tech oriented ones) I think GSL has turned into the language that I was looking for at the beginning of the year. I'm starting to use it in my day job. The guides and documentation have been written to make it easier for agents and LLMs to use and my casual use so far has shown some promise. It's still very much an experiment but I'd like to get other people to take a look and see if it's useful for them too. Have I even made the right assumptions and picked the right abstractions? Have you tried to do something like this yourself? You can begin with the "Getting Started" guide, the specs, or just jump right in to the flagship examples. "Example #3: Architecture Across Boundaries" is fairly close to what I wanted to do originally. https://github.com/dnnrly/gsl-lang

Pizza Bot is a self-hosted desktop app for Mac, Windows, and Linux that runs AI agents in the background and exposes them through an email-like UI. Finished work shows up in Unread, and anything waiting on your approval shows up in Action. It's Apache 2.0-licensed, there's no signup and no telemetry, and you bring your own model provider: Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a local model through Ollama. There are builds on the releases page, or you can run it from source. Pizza Bot started as an internal passion project I worked on with a small team at Amazon. The whole thing came out of my frustration at having to manually log CRM activities through a browser form. I built a simple REST API called "JoeBot" that connected to my authenticated browser session over CDP and filled out the form for me using Playwright. Then I hacked up a quick Obsidian plugin so I could trigger it from my local notes (no AI and no MCP servers involved). This caught on quickly. My fellow AWS Solutions Architect Igor Fil joined up with me, and we rebranded the project as "Pizza Bot," named after Amazon's two-pizza teams. We started seeing what other automations we could build. We found a GraphQL API we could query and hacked up some "recipes" to pull data out of the CRM to help with meeting prep. That worked great, and it was right around the time MCP servers seemed to be taking off, so we decided to expose Pizza Bot as an MCP server instead, so it would be available to AI tools through natural language. This was a decent solution for technical users, but the Account Managers who live inside our CRM system wanted something too. We decided to rebuild Pizza Bot as an Electron desktop app modeled after an email inbox, so it would be familiar to non-technical users and would run on both Mac and Windows. We also bundled internal MCP servers as OCI images and hosted them in Amazon ECR as an "addon marketplace" so users could install them with one click without having to set up Amazon developer tooling. The project took off organically and expanded outside of AWS into the wider Amazon organization globally. More than 2,000 people ended up using it for meeting prep, email drafting, Slack summaries, CRM logging, prioritizing their day, and web research. Once apps like Claude Cowork and Amazon's own Quick Desktop came out, we realized the real growth opportunity was outside of Amazon. Rather than try to rip out the Amazon-specific integrations, we rebuilt Pizza Bot once more as an open source project. We leaned on coding agents heavily, which is the only reason a team our size could pull off a full rewrite. I'm pleased to say it's finally public, and we're hoping to bring in community members and see where it goes. We'd like to do for knowledge workers what Claude Code and Codex have done for programmers. A couple of things to know up front. Most of what made Pizza Bot useful on day one inside Amazon came from that internal catalog of skills and MCP servers for Amazon's own systems, and none of it could come out with the app. So it ships thinner than the version those 2,000 people used, and building that catalog back up for tools other people actually use is where we need the most help. It's also a community project and not an AWS service, so there's no support or SLA behind it. The Windows and Linux builds aren't signed yet either. On the technical side, Pizza Bot is a server and a client. The desktop app bundles both, or you can point a client at a remote backend; personally, I self-host the server on my home network and reach it from my phone over Tailscale. The server owns the thread lifecycle and checkpoints state with DeepAgents and LangGraph, and clients rehydrate from it as needed, so you can disconnect mid-run and pick the thread back up from another client. Approval pauses outlive the session that created them and collect in an Action filter, so you can answer an hour later from a different device. The agent you talk to has a sandboxed QuickJS interpreter that can reach your filesystem only if you grant it a folder, but its main job is to delegate. Each subagent is a 1:1 mapping of a Skill, and an Activity bar shows that subagent and the tool calls it's making as it works. Memory is opt-in and stored as plain markdown files on your machine. Every tool call is explicit, including looking up a memory - we err on the side of transparency to reduce surprises. Tools come from MCP servers, and skills are ordinary SKILL.md files with a per-tool approval policy, so existing skills that don't require a code interpreter should still work. What I'd most like to hear about is where the app itself gets in your way, the kind of problem you can't fix by writing a skill or an MCP server. I'm around today to answer questions!

projects.author: hsluoyz

github.name: casdoor/casdoor
github.description: An open-source Agent-first Identity and Access Management (IAM) /LLM MCP & agent gateway and auth server with web UI supporting OpenClaw, MCP, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, CAS, LDAP, SCIM, WebAuthn, TOTP, MFA, Face ID, Google Workspace, Azure AD

projects.summary: Casdoor 是一个开源的身份认证与访问管理平台（IAM / SSO），Go + React 写的，Apache 2.0，14.4k star。9 月 1 日发布了 v4.0，到 9 月 9 日已经迭代到 v4.3；今年 2 月它进了 CNCF 云原生全景图（Provisioning → Security & Compliance）。 先说最有用的一条：如果你在写远程 MCP Server，鉴权这块可以不用自己做了。 MCP 规范要求远程 Server 用 OAuth 2.1 鉴权，但 Agent 客户端（Claude Code、Cursor 这些）事先根本不知道自己要向谁注册，所以动态客户端注册是绕不过去的一环。Casdoor 把这套备齐了：OAuth 2.1 + PKCE、RFC 7591 动态客户端注册（注册端点在 .well-known/openid-configuration 里公布，客户端自己能发现）、RFC 7592 客户端管理、授权同意页、JWKS 与 JWT 校验。你只要把自己 MCP Server 的 Protected Resource Metadata 指向 Casdoor，剩下的认证、同意、发 token、验 token 都不用写。 它自己也是个 MCP Server，暴露 15 个工具（user / application / permission 三类对象各一套 CRUD），Claude Code 接上去可以直接说「给这个组织加个用户」。再加上 OpenClaw 接入：Agent 运行时的 trace / metric / log 按 OTLP 推进来，落成可查的记录——身份、权限、审计连成一条线。 常规能力（这部分它做了五年）：同一份用户目录可以通过 OAuth 2.0、OIDC、SAML 2.0、CAS、LDAP、SCIM 2.0 访问，所以新写的 SPA 和只认 CAS 的老系统能共用一批账号；登录方式覆盖密码、邮箱短信验证码、WebAuthn / passkey、TOTP、Face ID，外加 Google、GitHub、Entra ID 等上百个身份源；组织、应用、登录页品牌化全在 Web 控制台改，不用改配置文件重新部署；授权规则交给 Casbin。部署就一个 Go 二进制加一个数据库，没有 JVM，没有 operator。 v4 这一轮：控制台从 Ant Design 整个换成 shadcn/ui（Vite 构建，注意静态资源路径从 build/static/{js,css} 变成了 build/assets/），登录注册页重做并修好了移动端；新增 OIDC 身份源类型；LDAP 自动同步改成只在单节点跑；支持 Redis Cluster；用户的角色和权限会标出各自由哪个组、哪个角色授予。 一条命令试： bash docker run -p 8000:8000 casbin/casdoor-all-in-one 打开 ，组织 built-in，用户名 admin，密码 123（内置 SQLite 和示例数据，仅供试用）。在线 CNCF 全景图条目：

projects.summary: EvalArc 是面向 AI 智能体的开源评测与验收工具。支持 Python／JavaScript 候选、TOML 套件、JUnit 和离线报告复核，保留每轮原始记录。交互实验室展示高分仍违反关键业务约束的案例；0.8.0 可下载完整套件证据，并离线复算原始配置、执行计划、验收规则和 JUnit；浏览器可分享到具体调用步骤。提供可筛选 HF Casebook 和中英文文档，现有演示为脚本对照。 亮点 把讨论定位到同一步： Copy evidence link 保存任务、对照实现、种子、案例与 trace 步骤。接收者打开同一观察点，键盘可从详情返回案例列表；受限剪贴板有手动复制入口。 失败可恢复：suite、重复尝试、前后比较和任务包可以分别重试；一个任务包不可用时仍可检查另一个。页面经过 320／390／1440 像素与键盘路径验证。 高分不代表完成：工单策略得 93.75% 却重复写备注；代码实现得 92.5% 却混淆 JSON true 与 1。可检查全部 15 种声明缺陷，以及三项 suite 作业、六条重复尝试和 167 条审计用例的数据表。 可复核交付：evalarc verify 不执行候选代码，重算单次、重复、对照和完整套件报告，包括 TOML、plan、五次尝试与 JUnit；--require-accepted 检查配置的验收规则，--require-resolved 另行要求任务完整通过。Python／JavaScript 参考实现共享任务约定。 本账号为维护者，项目与 AI 结对开发，采用 MIT 许可，处于研究预览阶段。现有展示来自已保存的公开开发任务和脚本 Docker 对照，不提供真实大模型排名或 RL 收益结论。离线一致性校验不等于重新运行评分器，也不认证报告作者；原始候选路径与计时仍是报告元数据。

projects.title: Show HN: Authorize MCP tool calls without giving agents the credentials
